title: Check, Mate & Stalemate
concept: Check means the king is attacked. Mate means it can't escape. Stalemate means nobody wins, so don't do it when you're winning!

glossary.definition: It's your move, your king is NOT in check, but you have no legal move at all. The game ends in a draw.

summary: Check: the king is attacked. Checkmate: attacked with no way out, game over. Stalemate: not attacked but no legal move, a draw. When you're winning, always leave the king a move until you can mate.

narration: Three words every chess player must know: check, checkmate and stalemate. Let's meet the first two.
Queen to d4 is CHECK: the queen attacks the king along the long diagonal. Black must get out of it right now.
The king escapes to g8. Check isn't the end of the world, as long as there's a way out.
Queen to d8 is CHECKMATE: the king is attacked, every square around it is covered by your queen and king, and nothing can block or capture. Game over!

guided.hint: Trace a line from each white piece. Does any of them hit the black king? If so, can the king step somewhere safe?
Is the black king attacked right now? Now look at every square it could step to.
guided.explanation: Stalemate! Black's king isn't attacked, but every square it could step to is covered by the queen or the king. No legal move means a draw: White was a whole queen up and still didn't win. When you're winning, always leave the king a square until you can mate.

guided.hint: The king is attacked. Can it run? Can anything block the rook, or capture it?
guided.explanation: Checkmate! The rook attacks the king along the back row, the king's own pawns block every escape, and nothing can block or capture the rook. You'll meet this one again: it's called a back-rank mate.
